objective: Rebuild Maples' playable world/map from first principles. The owner rejects the current environment as toy-like, cheap, low-effort and visually generic. Do not polish the existing circular diorama; use it only to preserve gameplay contracts. Replace the current flat disc/radial-prop/primitive-cliff language with an expensive, authored, artistic fantasy environment that feels like one real place from gameplay camera angles. Use textures and materially rich surface treatment as a core part of the redesign, not as an afterthought. The finished direction should feel commercially art-directed: asymmetrical macro terrain, memorable landmark hierarchy, layered depth, continuous terrain transitions, embedded ruins/nature/shrine, ecological foliage composition, deliberate negative space, believable surface scale, atmospheric separation and dense-but-controlled detail. Preserve Maples/Lumenwood identity while remaining original and not copying MapleStory, D&D or any other franchise.
role: principal environment artist, technical level artist, material artist and Three.js rendering engineer for a commercial-indie action RPG
relevant_context: Start strictly from current main fcd928cf43ff345eb9d09f0332ba79c64af39647 and ignore all older open world/map PRs as implementation sources. Current World.js visibly uses a cylinder/circle arena, flat-shaded primitive terrain, radial trees, uniform random rocks/plants/crystals and blocky procedural ruins. ShowcasePass surrounds it with repeated dodecahedron cliff shelves, cylinder terraces and cone mountains. EnvironmentAssets/NatureAssets add licensed KayKit/Quaternius GLBs but currently read as layers placed on top of the primitive base. The owner explicitly wants a from-zero environment rethink and explicitly requires textures. Preserve Rowan/enemy movement and combat authority, encounter coordinates, boss trigger, portal functionality/unlock behavior, camera/input/UI/progression, public asset-manager readiness/failure contracts, asset licensing, PerformancePass rebatching, NatureInstancing compatibility and mobile playability. Keep the central traversable gameplay surface mechanically compatible even if its visual terrain is completely re-authored around/over it. Use deterministic seeded composition. Reuse existing licensed assets where useful but recontextualize and material-tune them so the world does not read like an asset-pack showroom. For textures, prefer original procedural CanvasTexture/DataTexture/shader-generated detail or already-licensed local asset textures available through the existing GLBs. Build shared reusable material/texture resources; do not generate per-object textures. Use texture repeat/rotation/scale intentionally, correct color-space handling, anisotropy where supported, and quality-aware texture resolution. Aim for layered albedo/detail breakup and roughness/normal-like surface variation on soil, moss, worn stone, roots/wood and foliage. If a full normal map is impractical in the allowlist, implement convincing shader/procedural micro-normal or roughness variation rather than falling back to flat color. Avoid giant unique textures, web downloads, unlicensed images, runtime network dependencies, obvious tiling at gameplay distance, excessive bloom/emissive clutter, primitive silhouettes, evenly spaced radial layouts and unbounded allocations.
acceptance_criteria: The map no longer reads as a circular toy arena/diorama or a ring of evenly scattered props; the macro silhouette is authored, asymmetrical and intentional.

Remove, replace or convincingly bury/disguise the obvious cylinder ground, circle overlay, repeated cone mountains, dodecahedron cliff beads, cylinder terraces and icosahedron tree/cloud blob language rather than increasing primitive counts.
Create one dominant memorable environmental landmark plus secondary landmarks that establish a clear visual route and foreground/midground/background hierarchy.
The traversable combat space remains mechanically compatible, but visually reads as part of a larger continuous terrain formation instead of a flat arena disc.

Use textures materially: soil, moss/groundcover, worn stone, roots/wood and foliage must have visibly differentiated surface breakup through shared albedo/detail textures plus roughness and normal-like variation or equivalent shaders/procedural maps.

Texture resources are deterministic, reusable and performance-conscious: no per-frame regeneration, no per-object unique texture spam, sensible resolution caps, repeat/anisotropy/color-space handling and high/low quality budgets.
Ruins, shrine/portal, foliage and terrain feel embedded through grading, grounding, edge transitions, debris/roots/moss or terrain overlap instead of sitting on top of the map as separate props.

Foliage follows ecological clustering, edge framing, local density gradients and deliberate openings rather than uniform radial scatter; low quality preserves the same composition with reduced density.
Lighting and atmosphere create depth/focal hierarchy without depending on excessive emissive intensity; mobile/low quality remains readable.
Preserve portal position/functionality and all gameplay-critical coordinate contracts unless a purely decorative transform leaves mechanics unchanged.
Remain compatible with EnvironmentAssets, NatureAssets, PerformancePass rebatching and NatureInstancing; avoid unbounded allocations, per-frame geometry/material churn and excessive shadow casters.
Use deterministic seeded placement and expose testable composition/material budget constants or invariants.

Add focused tests in tests/world-art-direction-unit.mjs covering deterministic composition, texture/material budgets, high/low quality constraints and preservation of gameplay-critical world contracts.
Run all approved build/regression commands and report measured pass/fail results separately from visual assumptions. Identify any visual/performance checks that still require Sol/owner play-testing.
Return a bounded unified diff only inside the allowlist, with a concise visual/material rationale, performance risks, texture-memory considerations and validation notes for Sol review.
